Subject: Request: 5-year commitment + renewal protection / uplift cap — Kestrel Analytics

Team — quick ask: Kestrel (Prospect -> now close to signature) is requesting a 5-year committed package for our inference hosted API. Summary below and attachment (term_sheet_v3). I need an exec-level thumbs-up for the non-standard commercial asks so we can finalize DocuSign by next week.

Deal snapshot:
- Account: Kestrel Analytics (series B, health analytics)
- Term requested: 5 years (annual billing)
- Committed ARR: $2.4M (year 1 baseline) with 12% step-downs/consumption variance baked into model
- Requested commercial concessions: 5-year price lock (no price increase during term), renewal protection that limits renewal uplift to a max of 10% on the first renewal, and an uplift-cap (annual cap) of 6% thereafter
- Customer asks for audit rights and guaranteed data residency in us-west-2 (we already support)

Why this is sensitive: a 5-year hard price lock exposes us to inflation and model-cost increases. Legal flagged the renewal-protection language: they want explicit definition of what counts as "change in pricing" (new features vs unit price). Finance wants a guardrail if model execution costs increase >15%.

Request: Exec approval to accept the following binding commercial terms:
1) 5-year committed term with a fixed unit price for the first 48 months (4 years) and an indexed protection mechanism for year 5 capped at 6%
2) Renewal protection: customer cannot be charged >10% increase at first renewal if they maintain >=85% of committed consumption in year 5
3) Uplift cap: annual price increases limited to 6% after year 4 (if auto-renewed), with an explicit carveout for material hardware-cost pass-throughs (requires finance sign-off)

Attachments: KESTREL_term_sheet_v3.pdf (term sheet), KESTREL_redline_legal.docx (customer redlines).

Please advise approval, veto, or alternate language by EOD Monday — procurement is timeboxed.

Thanks,
Nikhil
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Nikhil — read and noted. A few quick thoughts:
- Full 5-year hard price lock feels like too much exposure. Agree with finance/legal concerns.
- Alternative we should consider: 4-year fixed + optional 1-year extension at pre-agreed indexation (cap 6%) tied to cloud/hardware cost index. That limits our tail risk and gives customer near-longterm certainty.
- If we must do 5-year: require consumption minimums and an exit right or reconciliation clause if our per-token execution cost increases >15% (pass-through or credit). Also require a revenue protection clause (customer must maintain >=80% of committed ARR or we can reprice).

Happy to support escalation. Legal: please review the redline and advise on precise language for the "material cost increase" carveout. Marissa: please flag for Deal Desk templating if we end up approving.
